book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 4 · Medical and Legal Issues
title: Law, Accountability and Scope: Your Legal Framework
next: Chapter 4, Lesson 2: Negligence, consent, refusal and the PCR

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already work under a licence, follow protocols, ask before you touch and write a PCR. Today, as a PCP:

  1. How the law reaches you: civil vs criminal, and key torts
  2. Who you answer to, and how medical control works
  3. Scope of practice vs standard of care, and privacy

Textbook: Chapter 4, PDF pages 220–242
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already practise under a licence: you follow protocols, ask before you touch a patient, and write a report on every call. So the law is not new to you. What changes is how much rides on your decisions. As a PCP you can do more, so there's more you can get wrong, and you'll be judged as a PCP. Today we'll cover how Canadian law reaches a paramedic, who you answer to and how medical control works, and the difference between scope of practice and standard of care, plus privacy.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经在执照下执业：按流程做事、碰病人之前先征得同意、每次出车都写报告。所以法律对你们并不陌生。变的是你的决定分量更重了。作为 PCP 你能做的更多，可能出错的地方也更多，而且别人会用 PCP 的标准来衡量你。今天讲：加拿大的法律怎样管到 paramedic；你要向谁负责、医疗指导怎么运作；执业范围和照护标准的区别，以及隐私保护。

slides.title: Law vs ethics: four kinds of trouble
slides.body:
Laws are enforceable; ethics are not

  • A lawsuit (civil liability)
  • Criminal charges
  • A disciplinary hearing with your regulator
  • Action by your employer or medical director

Best protection: careful assessment, appropriate care, and complete, accurate documentation.
slides.say: First, a quick distinction. Ethics are ideas about right and wrong; laws are rules with penalties that can be enforced. On every call you work inside several layers of law: emergency driving rules, EMS and licensing laws, civil and criminal law about touching and moving people, and privacy laws such as PIPEDA, the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act. Most paramedic law is provincial, because health care is provincial. Break these laws and four kinds of trouble can follow, shown here. Your best protection is good practice: assess carefully, treat appropriately, and document completely.
slides.sayZh: 先分清一个概念。伦理是关于对错的观念；法律是有强制处罚的规则。每次出车，你都在好几层法律之内工作：急救驾驶规则、EMS 和执照法律、关于触碰和搬运他人的民事与刑事法，还有隐私法，比如 PIPEDA（Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act）。管 paramedic 的法律大多是省级的，因为医疗卫生归省管。违反这些法律，可能带来屏幕上这四种麻烦。最好的保护就是把事情做好：仔细评估、恰当处置、完整记录。

slides.title: Civil vs criminal law
slides.body:
CivilCriminal
Who actsPatient sues (plaintiff)Government prosecutes
ProofMost believable evidenceBeyond reasonable doubt
ResultDamages (money)Fine, prison, or both
ExampleMalpractice suitAssault, unsafe driving

One act can lead to both. A bad outcome alone does not prove negligence.
slides.say: Two kinds of law can bring you to court. In civil law, the patient or the family sues you. They're the plaintiff, you're the defendant, and they usually want money, called damages. They win if most of the believable evidence is on their side. Malpractice suits are civil. In criminal law, the government prosecutes and must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, a much higher bar; the penalty can be a fine, prison, or both. One act, like a wrongful restraint, can lead to both kinds of case. But a bad outcome alone doesn't prove negligence. The patient must prove every element, which we'll cover next lesson.
slides.sayZh: 有两类法律可能把你带上法庭。民事法里，病人或家属起诉你：他们是原告，你是被告，通常要的是钱，叫损害赔偿；只要大部分可信证据对他们有利就能胜诉。医疗过失诉讼就是民事。刑事法里，是政府起诉，必须证明到排除合理怀疑，门槛高得多，处罚可以是罚款、监禁或两者并处。同一个行为，比如不当约束，可能同时引来两种官司。但结局不好本身并不证明有过失，病人必须证明每一个要素，下节课讲。

slides.title: Torts you could commit on a call
slides.body:
Assaultmaking someone fear harmno touch needed
Batterytouching without consentharmful or offensive
False imprisonmentholding someone against their willwithout a lawful reason

Defamation: libel is written (your PCR); slander is spoken (your handover). Describe, don't label.
slides.say: A tort is a wrong that you can be sued for. Four matter most. Assault is making someone fear they're about to be hurt; no touch is needed. Battery is touching someone in a harmful or offensive way without consent. False imprisonment is holding someone against their will without a lawful reason, like transporting a capable adult who said no. Defamation is a false statement that damages a reputation: libel if written, as in a PCR, and slander if spoken, as at handover. Why it matters more now: almost any treatment without consent can be assault, battery, or both, and as a PCP you offer many more treatments.
slides.sayZh: 侵权是可以被人起诉的不法行为。最相关的有四种。Assault（威胁/攻击）是让人害怕自己马上要受伤，不需要碰到对方。Battery（非法接触）是未经同意、以有害或冒犯的方式碰了对方。非法拘禁是没有合法理由违背他人意愿把人扣住，比如把说了「不」的有能力成年人强行送走。诽谤是损害他人名誉的不实陈述：写下来的叫 libel，比如写在 PCR 里；说出来的叫 slander，比如交接时的话。为什么现在更重要？几乎任何未经同意的治疗都可能构成 assault、battery 或两者，而作为 PCP，你提供的治疗多得多。

slides.q: A PCP starts an IV on an alert, capable patient who clearly said "no needles." The IV goes in with no problems. Which statement is true?
options: There's no legal issue because no harm was done
It may be battery: he was touched without consent
Only the employer can be held responsible
It's slander, because his wishes were ignored
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A PCP starts an IV on an alert, capable patient who clearly said no needles. The IV goes in with no problems. Which statement is true? A, there's no legal issue because no harm was done. B, it may be battery, because he was touched without consent. C, only the employer can be held responsible. D, it's slander, because his wishes were ignored. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一名 PCP 给一位清醒、有决策能力、明确说了「不要打针」的病人开了静脉，过程很顺利。下面哪句话是对的？A 没有造成伤害，所以没有法律问题；B 可能构成 battery，因为他在未经同意的情况下被触碰；C 只有雇主需要负责；D 这是 slander，因为他的意愿被忽视了。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Battery is touching someone in a harmful or offensive way without consent, and an unwanted needle fits, even if it goes in perfectly. A is wrong because battery doesn't need a bad outcome. C is wrong: under vicarious liability the employer usually pays, but the paramedic stays personally liable. D is wrong because slander is a false spoken statement that hurts someone's reputation.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。Battery 是未经同意以有害或冒犯的方式触碰他人，病人不想要的一针就属于这种情况，哪怕扎得再顺利。A 错，battery 不需要有坏结局；C 错，按替代责任通常由雇主赔偿，但 paramedic 本人仍负个人责任；D 错，slander 是损害他人名誉的不实口头陈述。

slides.title: Where lawsuits come from
slides.body:
• No-transport calls: the patient stays home, then gets worse
  • Quality of care: a missed treatment, or a harmful one
  • Ambulance collisions
Claim filed→Discovery: months to 2+ years→Settlement or trial

A suit can start years after the call. Your PCR is your memory.
slides.say: Where do lawsuits against paramedics come from? Three main areas. First, no-transport calls, where the patient stayed home and got worse, or the response was delayed. A signed refusal form, on its own, doesn't protect you. Second, quality of care: a treatment you missed, or one you shouldn't have given. Third, ambulance collisions. Lawsuits are slow. After the claim comes discovery, when both sides exchange questions, records and sworn statements, for a few months to over two years. Most cases settle before trial. Since a suit can start years after the call, your PCR must tell the story. And courtesy and honesty prevent most complaints.
slides.sayZh: 针对 paramedic 的诉讼通常来自哪里？三个方面。第一，没有转运的呼叫：病人留在家里后来恶化，或者响应延误。光有一张签了字的拒绝书，并不能保护你。第二，照护质量：漏做了治疗，或者做了不该做的。第三，急救车碰撞。诉讼很漫长：起诉之后是证据开示期，双方交换书面问题、病历和宣誓证词，可能几个月到两年以上。大多数案子在开庭前和解。官司可能在出车好几年后才开始，所以你的 PCR 必须替你讲清楚经过。另外，礼貌和诚实能避免大多数投诉。

slides.title: Three lines of accountability
slides.body:
Medical directoroversees your clinical practicecan restrict you or require retraining
Licensing bodygrants your licencecan act on it
Employerruns your jobcan discipline you

Some skills are done only as delegated by a physician, but your actions are still your own.
slides.say: Who do you answer to? The book describes three lines of accountability: your medical director, who oversees your clinical practice; your licensing body, which grants your licence; and your employer. They overlap, but they're separate. Provincial law often allows certain advanced skills only when a physician delegates them to you. Even then, your actions are your own. The medical director can be held responsible for poor supervision, and can restrict your practice, withdraw supervision, or require retraining. Employer discipline is a separate matter. As your skills grow from EMR to PCP, more of your work runs under this medical oversight.
slides.sayZh: 你要向谁负责？书里讲三条问责线：医疗主管，监督你的临床执业；执照机构，发给你执照；还有雇主。三者有重叠，但各自独立。省法律常规定，某些高级技能只能在医生委派下操作。即便如此，你的行为仍是你自己的。医疗主管可能因监督不力被追责，可以限制你的执业、撤回监督或要求补训；雇主的纪律处分是另一回事。从 EMR 升到 PCP，技能变多，你更多的工作处在这种医疗监督之下。

slides.title: Medical control and doctors on scene
slides.body:
Direct medical controlIndirect medical control
Live orders by phone or radioProtocols, standing orders, guidelines
  • Refuse an order only if you truly believe it will harm the patient
  • Must leave a protocol? Call direct medical control, then document
  • Doctor on scene: confirm a provincial licence; record name and contact
  • If they act outside your protocols or take over, they ride in
slides.say: Medical control comes in two forms. Direct medical control is a physician giving orders live, by phone or radio. Indirect medical control is written ahead of time: protocols, standing orders and guidelines. You can't simply ignore a physician's order; refuse only if you truly believe it will harm the patient. If an unusual situation forces you off a protocol, call direct medical control and document it. If a doctor at the scene offers help, confirm a provincial licence and record their name and contact. If they go outside your protocols or take over care, they ride in. Disagreements go to direct medical control, not to you.
slides.sayZh: 医疗指导分两种。直接医疗指导是医生通过电话或无线电实时给医嘱；间接医疗指导是事先写好的：流程、常规医嘱和指南。医生的医嘱不能随便不理，只有在你真心认为它会伤害病人时才可以拒绝。特殊情况逼你偏离流程时，联系直接医疗指导并记录下来。现场有医生主动帮忙，先确认他持有本省执照，记下姓名和联系方式。如果他做了超出你们流程的事，或接管了照护，就要随车去医院。意见不合时，由直接医疗指导裁决，而不是你。

slides.title: Scope of practice vs standard of care
slides.body:
Scope of practiceStandard of care
What your licence allowsWhat a reasonable paramedic would do
Set by provincial laws and regulationsSame training, same situation
Your medical director can narrow itShown by experts, protocols, your PCR

Outside your scope: possible negligence, in some provinces a crime. A licence is a privilege, not a right.
slides.say: Don't mix up these two. Scope of practice is what your licence allows. It comes from provincial EMS laws and regulations, which list each level's skills and drugs, and your medical director can narrow it. The book also names a shared law for many health professions: the Health Professions Act in Alberta or British Columbia. Working outside your scope may be negligence, in some provinces even a crime. Standard of care is what a reasonable paramedic with similar training would do in the same situation. You can be inside your scope and still below the standard, by doing the right skill badly or too late.
slides.sayZh: 这两个概念别混淆。执业范围是执照允许你做的事，来自省级 EMS 法律和条例，里面列出每个级别的技能和药物；医疗主管还可以再收窄。书里还提到一部管很多医疗职业的共同法律：Alberta 或 British Columbia 的 Health Professions Act。超出执业范围操作可能构成过失，在某些省甚至是犯罪。照护标准是一名受过相似训练的合理 paramedic 在相同情况下会怎么做。你可能在范围之内，却仍低于标准，比如技能做得不好或做得太晚。

slides.title: Privacy: guard the patient's information
slides.body:
• PIPEDA or a provincial law: criminal and civil penalties
  • Share only what treatment or administration needs
  • PCRs: never lost, never left unsecured
  • No case talk in elevators, cafés or on social media
  • A subpoena goes to your privacy officer first
  • Patients may see their record and ask for corrections
slides.say: Privacy laws protect health information, and breaking them can bring criminal and civil penalties. Share information only when treatment or your service's administration needs it. Keep PCRs secure; only the staff who take over care, and authorised people in your service, should see them. Don't discuss a case where others can hear, like an elevator or a coffee shop. On social media, post nothing that could identify a patient: no scene photos, no call stories, no pictures of an X-ray. A subpoena, which is a legal demand for records, goes to your privacy officer. And patients may see their own information and ask for corrections.
slides.sayZh: 隐私法保护健康信息，违反了可能面临刑事和民事处罚。只有治疗或机构行政需要时才分享信息。PCR 要妥善保管，只有接手照护的医护人员和机构内获授权的人可以看。不要在别人听得到的地方讨论病例，比如电梯或咖啡店。社交媒体上不能发任何可能识别出病人的内容：现场照片、出车故事、X 光片照片都不行。传票，也就是调取记录的法律文书，要交给隐私官处理。病人本人可以查看自己的信息并要求更正。

slides.q: You're a PCP on an interfacility transfer. The patient has an infusion you are not licensed to manage. The sending doctor says, "You'll be fine, just watch it." What should you do?
options: Take the patient and manage it as best you can
Stop the infusion once you're in the ambulance
Tell the sending staff it's outside your scope and call direct medical control
Refuse and leave without discussing it
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. On an interfacility transfer, your patient has an infusion you aren't licensed to manage. The sending doctor says, you'll be fine, just watch it. What should you do? A, take the patient and manage it as best you can. B, stop the infusion once you're in the ambulance. C, tell the sending staff it's outside your scope, and call direct medical control. D, refuse and leave without discussing it. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。院际转运时，病人身上有一路你没有执照管理的输注。转出医院的医生说：「没事的，看着点就行。」你该怎么做？A 接走病人，尽力管理；B 上车后把输注停掉；C 告诉转出医院人员这超出你的执业范围，并联系直接医疗指导；D 拒绝，不作任何沟通就离开。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. When a transfer patient needs care outside your scope, raise it with the sending staff and contact direct medical control; the sending hospital must provide properly trained staff. A puts you outside your scope, which can be negligence. B changes the treatment without an order and could harm the patient. D leaves the problem unsolved; your job is to advocate for the patient.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。转运病人需要超出你执业范围的处置时，要向转出医院人员提出，并联系直接医疗指导；派受过相应训练的人员随行是转出医院的责任。A 让你超范围执业，可能构成过失；B 没有医嘱就改变治疗，可能伤害病人；D 问题没解决，而你的职责是为病人代言。

slides.title: Off duty: Good Samaritan and other shields
slides.body:
• Off duty, most provinces don't force you to stop
  • Once you start: meet the standard, don't abandon
  • Each province has its own act (BC: Good Samaritan Act)
  • Covers help that is voluntary and unpaid
  • Never covers gross negligence; not for on-duty work
  • On duty, your employer usually pays: vicarious liability
slides.say: What if you stop at a crash on your day off? Most provinces don't force you to stop; Quebec is the exception. But once you start, you must meet the standard of care and stay until on-duty crews take over. Each province has its own protection law; the book names the Good Samaritan Acts of Ontario and British Columbia, and Alberta's Emergency Medical Aid Act. They cover voluntary, unpaid help, but never gross negligence, such as a procedure you aren't trained or certified for. On duty they don't apply; instead your employer is usually liable, called vicarious liability, though you stay personally liable too.
slides.sayZh: 如果你休息日路过车祸停下来帮忙呢？大多数省份不强制你停下，Quebec 是例外。但一旦开始施救，你就必须达到照护标准，并守到当班人员接手。每个省有自己的保护法；书里列了 Ontario 和 British Columbia 各自的 Good Samaritan Act，以及 Alberta 的 Emergency Medical Aid Act。它们保护自愿、无偿的帮助，但从不保护重大过失，比如做你没受过训练或没取得资格的操作。当班时这些法律不适用，通常由雇主承担责任，叫替代责任，但你本人仍负个人责任。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• You're judged against a reasonable PCP, not an EMR
  • Know your exact scope, plus any limits from your medical director
  • More of your work runs under medical oversight and delegation
  • Leaving a protocol? Call direct medical control, write why
  • Before a transfer, check the patient's needs fit your scope
  • Each new treatment you offer needs consent
slides.say: So what changes for you as a PCP? First, the standard of care follows your training: a court asks what a reasonable PCP would have done, not what an EMR would have done. Second, know your exact scope, including any limits from your medical director, because acting outside it can be negligence. Third, more of your work runs under medical oversight: protocols, delegated skills, and calls to direct medical control. If you must leave a protocol, call first and document it. Fourth, before a transfer, check that the patient's needs fit your scope. And each new treatment you offer, like an IV, is another touch that needs permission.
slides.sayZh: 那么作为 PCP 有什么不同？第一，照护标准跟着你的训练走：法庭问的是一名合理的 PCP 会怎么做，而不是 EMR。第二，准确掌握你的执业范围，包括医疗主管设的限制，因为超范围操作可能构成过失。第三，你更多的工作处在医疗监督之下：流程、委派的技能、给直接医疗指导打电话。必须偏离流程时，先打电话再记录。第四，转运出发前，确认病人的需要在你的范围之内。还有，你提供的每一项新治疗，比如静脉通路，都是又一次需要许可的触碰。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A transfer needing care beyond PCP scope: speak up first
  • An order that seems unsafe: clarify, don't just comply
  • A doctor on scene who goes past your protocols but won't ride in
  • Off duty: skills you aren't certified for = gross negligence risk
  • Lights and sirens never excuse unsafe driving
  • Any photo or post that could identify a patient
slides.say: Here are the legal traps that grow with your scope. On a transfer, if the patient needs care beyond PCP scope, or seems unstable, tell the sending staff and call direct medical control before you leave. If any doctor gives you an order that seems unsafe, ask for clarification; you're accountable for what you do. A doctor on scene who goes beyond your protocols must ride in. Off duty, stick to what you're trained and certified for, or you risk a finding of gross negligence. Lights and sirens never allow unsafe driving; a driver can face criminal charges. And keep patients off social media.
slides.sayZh: 下面是随执业范围扩大而增多的法律陷阱。转运时，如果病人需要 PCP 范围以外的处置，或看起来不稳定，出发前就告诉转出医院人员并联系直接医疗指导。任何医生给你看起来不安全的医嘱，都要请他澄清，因为你要为自己做的事负责。现场医生做了超出你们流程的事，就必须随车。休息时只做你受过训练、取得资格的操作，否则可能被判重大过失。警灯警笛从不允许危险驾驶，司机可能因此被刑事起诉。另外，病人的信息不要上社交媒体。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Every EMR and PCP candidate must pass the jurisprudence exam
  • 25 questions, no time limit, 80% to pass
  • PCP written exam: the COPR entry-to-practice exam
  • PCP practical: one medical + one trauma scenario
  • In BC, EMRs have no IV access; the IV is PCP scope

The book's legal examples are often from Ontario. Learn BC's rules.
slides.say: Some facts from the BC exam guidelines. Every licensing candidate, EMR or PCP, must pass the jurisprudence exam from EMALB, the Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board: twenty-five questions, no time limit, eighty percent to pass, and after a second fail, a five-day wait before the third and final try. Your PCP written exam is the COPR entry-to-practice exam; your practical exam is one medical and one trauma scenario. And the scope line: in BC, EMRs have no IV access, so the IV is yours as a PCP. The book often uses Ontario examples, so learn BC's rules.
slides.sayZh: 几条来自 BC 考试指南的事实。每位申请执照的考生，不论 EMR 还是 PCP，都必须通过 EMALB（Emergency Medical Assistants Licensing Board）的法规考试，也就是 jurisprudence exam：二十五题，不限时，八十分及格；第二次没过，要等五天才能考第三次，也是最后一次。PCP 的笔试是 COPR 的执业准入考试；实操考试是一个内科场景和一个创伤场景。还有范围界线：在 BC，EMR 没有静脉通路权限，开静脉是你作为 PCP 的事。教材常用 Ontario 的例子，所以要学 BC 的规则。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Civil: patient sues for money. Criminal: the state, beyond reasonable doubt
  2. You answer to your medical director, licensing body and employer
  3. Scope = what you may do; standard of care = what a reasonable PCP would do

Next: negligence, consent, refusal and the PCR
slides.say: Let's wrap up. One: civil law is a patient suing for money, decided on the weight of the evidence; criminal law is the government prosecuting, proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Treatment without consent can be battery. Two: you answer to your medical director, your licensing body and your employer, and your actions are your own, even when a skill is delegated. Three: scope of practice is what your licence lets you do; standard of care is what a reasonable PCP would do. Meet both. Next lesson: negligence, consent and refusal, restraint, and a PCR that protects you. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，民事法是病人为索赔起诉你，看证据倾向；刑事法是政府起诉，要排除合理怀疑。未经同意的治疗可能构成 battery。二，你向医疗主管、执照机构和雇主负责；即使技能是委派的，你的行为仍是你自己的。三，执业范围是执照允许你做什么，照护标准是一名合理的 PCP 会怎么做，两样都要达到。下节课讲过失、同意与拒绝、约束，以及一份能保护你的 PCR。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
